A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LinVideo and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across layout changes and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-generation evaluations, latency measurements, ablations, and qualitative examples using Wan models.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds four-step baseline comparisons, CogVideoX evaluations, SLA comparisons, and kernel and training-cost results.

M1.justification: The Hedgehog kernel, selective layer transfer, constraint and regularization losses, ADM objective, and optional subsequent DMD2 distillation remain unchanged. Alternative kernels are evaluated as ablations rather than introduced into the proposed method.

E1.justification: OpenVid prompts and the VBench and VBench-2.0 text-to-video evaluation coverage are retained. CogVideoX-2B adds a model configuration, not a new dataset or task; the added distillation and hardware comparisons likewise retain existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 explicitly excludes SLA, whereas v3 evaluates it in Table VI. Table III also adds four-step DMD2 versions of FA2, DFA, XAttn, SVG, and SVG2 as comparators, substantially expanding the direct comparisons for the distilled LinVideo model.

E3.justification: Added experiments compare all methods under four-step DMD2, evaluate CogVideoX-2B, and benchmark SLA and LinVideo on both H100 and RTX5090. v3 also introduces an average of the selected VBench dimensions and training-FLOPs reporting. The previously reported Wan training and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table VII adds a focused kernel ablation comparing Hedgehog, ReLU, and Taylor expansion. Table IV supplements the existing training-time analysis with FLOPs. Earlier layer-selection, target-count, loss, alpha, temporal-jitter, and distillation-order analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-training-run uncertainty. v3 adds no seed or repeated-run reporting, and the existing per-prompt sampling counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained, while Tables III–VII add substantial comparative evidence. Four-step LinVideo reports 66.98 VBench at 6.11 seconds versus FA2's 67.68 at 8.76 seconds. On CogVideoX-2B, both score 65.97, with latencies of 29.64 and 41.35 seconds. SLA scores 65.72 versus LinVideo's 67.61, but is faster on RTX5090: 78.42 versus 112.14 seconds. Kernel and training-FLOPs results are also added.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix D score-difference derivation are retained. Correcting the model symbol to the hatted student in Section 5.3 does not alter the established mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about data-free linearization, selective transfer, ADM, and acceleration. The headline 1.43–1.71× and 15.9–20.9× speedups are unchanged.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion explains the Hedgehog choice through spiky weights and dot-product monotonicity, asserts applicability beyond a specific architecture following the CogVideoX evaluation, and elaborates the hardware-kernel explanation for SLA's speed. Existing interpretations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies LinVideo's PyTorch implementation and documents H100 versus RTX5090 measurements for the SLA comparison, alongside additional training-compute information. Existing Appendix A hyperparameters, data preparation, and sampling details are unchanged; detailed adaptation settings for the new comparisons remain sparse.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to TFMQ-DM, Temporal Feature Matters, Harmonica, QvGen, and Light Forcing. These modestly extend the acceleration and quantization context; the central positioning against pretraining approaches and SLA's intra-layer mixed attention remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely unchanged. Local edits add cross-references, correct model notation, revise correspondence information, and add acknowledgements. New appendix Sections H–K precede the existing visualization section, which moves from H to L.

P2.justification: Five compact appendix tables, III–VII, are added, with accompanying caption cross-references and local layout changes. Existing figures, qualitative images, and earlier table structures are preserved; the visualization pages are relocated rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The matched four-step controls and previously excluded SLA comparison improve the assessment of acceleration, while CogVideoX and kernel tests strengthen empirical support. The added results expose meaningful quality–latency tradeoffs. Benefits are limited by brief new protocol descriptions and Section H's unqualified 'outperforms all baselines' wording, despite FA2's higher VBench score in Table III. Overall, v3 provides better validation without resolving a fundamental defect in the retained work.
